title: Slot consolidation sprint: hypothesis jam and experiment plan
body:
Context:
We are seeing continued fragmentation of available GPU slots across regions during low-mid traffic windows. Small-duration bursts (2–15m) repeatedly allocate many tiny slots which increases coldstarts, KV-cache misses, and reduces effective packing density. Current autoscaler and slot allocator treat each customer pool as separate until capacity backfills, which leaves transient idle GPUs with 10-25% util for tens of minutes.

This doc is a working jam from the capacity squad + scheduler engineers to capture the slot consolidation hypothesis, quick simulation results, proposed experiments and rollout guardrails. Not final — rough notes and TODOs inside.

Attendees (sprint jam):
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Miguel Ortega (scheduler)
- Riley Chen (fleet-ops)
- Samira Khan (telemetry/observability)
- Jonah Weiss (SRE)
- Vlad (guest, product-hosted-api) - 30m

Observations motivating this:
1) Fragmentation metric: median per-node free-GPU-slices increased 18% week-over-week in NA-west during 01:00–06:00 UTC window (telemetry capture).
2) Coldstart correlation: requests that hit nodes with <40% active cache warmup see +25–40ms p95 token latency and 2–3x initial token GPU cycles.
3) Billing leak: small slot churn causes transient tiny billing increments & reduces batching efficiency — estimated 3.5% unit-cost overhead for hosted models at low traffic hours.

Hypothesis:
If we proactively consolidate ephemeral small allocations into shared packing slots (short-lived tenancy multiplexing with prewarmed KV caches), we will reduce coldstarts, increase average batch sizes during bursts, and lower per-token cost without materially increasing tail latency for strict single-tenant reserved workloads.

Design sketch / experiment variants:
A) Soft-consolidation (non-invasive): allow cross-tenant packing only for "best-effort" pools with <1% SLA-critical requests. Scheduler sets a 3-minute tenant-low-priority lease where a small number of different customers can share prewarmed contexts.
B) Prewarm-proactive: keep a small number of prewarmed shared slots in each AZ during low usage (target 1-2 per 100 active GPUs). These slots maintain common model KV caches for top-10 hosted models.
C) Backfill-fuse: when a node would otherwise be idle for >4 minutes, scheduler backfills with thin shared slices that accept very small sequential requests, then release back to dedicated tenancy on demand.

Simulation quick-capture (local sim v0.3):
- Input: traces from NA-west (7 days), 10k req/day baseline, typical burst profile (median burst 30s).
- Metric: average batch size, coldstart events per 1000 requests, p95 token latency delta, gpu-util efficiency.
- Results (rough):
  * Soft-consolidation: +22% avg batch size, -37% coldstarts, p95 latency +3ms on heavy single-tenant tails
  * Prewarm-proactive: +14% avg batch size, -25% coldstarts, operator cost +0.8% due to prewarm idle time
  * Backfill-fuse: +30% avg batch size during 00:00–06:00 window, -47% coldstarts, some transient 50–100ms higher latency for rare long-sequence single-tenant workloads

Risks & unknowns:
- Multi-tenant correctness: need review for data isolation and model KV contamination risk. Work with security/compliance (Samira to escalate) to confirm no leakage vectors.
- SLA violation surface: even small p95 increases are unacceptable for reserved Dedicated customers; must ensure reserved capacity never participates in consolidation.
- Accounting and billing: shared slot billing attribution design is required to avoid double-charging customers or under-crediting reserved pools. Finance ticket needed.
- Model determinism: some model variants have large warmup costs that are not amortized by short-shared slots. Need model-level metadata to opt-out.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- A1: Define pool labeling and opt-out annotation for reserved pools (owner: Asha) — spec by 2026-04-23.
- A2: Prototype scheduler policy patch for soft-consolidation (owner: Miguel) — small PR for canary in staging by 2026-04-28.
- A3: Telemetry dashboard: fragmentation index, consolidation participation, cost delta (owner: Samira) — dashboard mock by 2026-04-22, ingest hooks by 2026-04-30.
- A4: Security review kickoff (owner: Samira + security) — request created INFRA-7892, meeting scheduled 2026-04-23.
- A5: Cost/accounting rubric doc for shared-slot billing (owner: Riley) — draft to finance by 2026-04-26.
- A6: Canary rollout plan (owner: Jonah) — propose regions + size (start NA-west small) by 2026-04-27.

Rollout guardrails / rollback criteria:
- Start in staging with synthetic traffic; require coldstart events reduction >=25% with p95 token latency change <= +5ms for hosted best-effort pools.
- Canary in NA-west for 48 hours: if end-to-end error rate increases >0.1% or p99 latency for reserved pools increases >1%, immediate rollback.
- If billing attribution mismatches detected in initial 24h of canary, wait and fix (do not expand).

Open questions (to resolve in design doc):
- What is the canonical model metadata field for warmup-cost/opt-out? (Riley + Miguel)
- Should backfill-fuse include aggressive preemption hooks to return to single-tenant binding instantly? If so, what latency budget is acceptable? (Jonah)
- How to present shared-slot usage to customers in Console (transparency vs noise)? (Product + Asha)

Notes / rough TODOs:
- Add stitch-test to cluster-scheduler bench that simulates 50 mixed-tenancy customers and measures KV cache miss rate. (Miguel)
- Quick spike to measure cross-AZ prewarm inefficacy (Riley)
- Draft a short FAQ for CS explaining benefit and opt-out process (Samira + CS)

Decisions today:
- Proceed to implement Soft-consolidation prototype in staging (agreed).
- Reserve prewarm-proactive for follow-up after staging results (need cost analysis).

Appendix: telemetry snippets (copied):
- Query: fragmentation_index = count_if(node.free_slices>0)/node_count -> last week: 0.18 -> this week: 0.21 in NA-west
- Coldstart events: p95 initial token time for small-slices = 120ms (with warm cache ~70ms)

Slack notes: dropping the scheduler patch in #infra-sched and tagging @miguel. Will link PR once opened.

-- end working jam --

(Will convert to a clean proposal doc after initial prototype results and security check.)
